lines.raw: Grouper results are only as reliable as the **version** used and the **codes, flags and claims** fed in, so check those before you trust any DRG, APC, category or episode count.
lines.say: Grouper results are only as reliable as the version used and the codes, flags and claims fed in, so check those before you trust any D R G, A P C, category or episode count.

lines.raw: Problem 1: grouper versions.
lines.say: Problem 1: grouper versions.

lines.raw: How often the main groupers change.
lines.say: How often the main groupers change.

lines.raw: MS-DRG. New version starts: Every **1 October**, the start of the US government's fiscal year (FY): FY2025 began on 1 October 2024. Which version applies to a claim: The version in effect on the **discharge date**.
lines.say: M S DRG. New version starts: Every 1 October, the start of the U S government's fiscal year (F Y): F Y 2 0 2 5 began on 1 October 2024. Which version applies to a claim: The version in effect on the discharge date.

lines.raw: APC (OPPS). New version starts: Every **1 January**, with quarterly updates. Which version applies to a claim: The version in effect on the **service date**.
lines.say: A P C (O P P S). New version starts: Every 1 January, with quarterly updates. Which version applies to a claim: The version in effect on the service date.

lines.raw: ICD-10-CM / PCS codes. New version starts: Every **1 October** (plus occasional 1 April updates). Which version applies to a claim: Codes valid on the service or discharge date.
lines.say: I C D 10-CM or P C S codes. New version starts: Every 1 October (plus occasional 1 April updates). Which version applies to a claim: Codes valid on the service or discharge date.

lines.raw: CCSR, HCC and episode groupers. New version starts: Usually yearly. Which version applies to a claim: Depends on the use: see below.
lines.say: C C S R, H C C and episode groupers. New version starts: Usually yearly. Which version applies to a claim: Depends on the use: see below.

lines.raw: In the US: Which version should you use?
lines.say: In the U S: Which version should you use?

lines.raw: **To check or replicate a payment**: use the version in effect for the claim's date.
lines.say: To check or replicate a payment: use the version in effect for the claim's date.

lines.raw: A stay discharged on 28 September 2024 uses the FY2024 MS-DRG version; one discharged on 2 October 2024 uses FY2025.
lines.say: A stay discharged on 28 September 2024 uses the F Y 2 0 2 4 M S DRG version; one discharged on 2 October 2024 uses F Y 2 0 2 5.

lines.raw: A different version can give a different DRG and so a different price.
lines.say: A different version can give a different D R G and so a different price.

lines.raw: **To study a trend over years**: regroup **every year with one version**, so a change in the rulebook does not look like a change in care.
lines.say: To study a trend over years: regroup every year with one version, so a change in the rulebook does not look like a change in care.

lines.raw: Real example: in FY2024 (from 1 October 2023), Medicare created new MS-DRGs for hip replacement after a **hip fracture**, taking those stays out of the general hip and knee replacement DRGs.
lines.say: Real example: in F Y 2 0 2 4 (from 1 October 2023), Medicare created new M S DRGs for hip replacement after a hip fracture, taking those stays out of the general hip and knee replacement D R G's.

lines.raw: Counted with each year's own version, the old DRGs suddenly "lost" stays.
lines.say: Counted with each year's own version, the old D R G's suddenly "lost" stays.

lines.raw: Problem 2: bad inputs.
lines.say: Problem 2: bad inputs.

lines.raw: Input problems and what they do.
lines.say: Input problems and what they do.

lines.raw: **Missing or invalid POA flag**. What happens: The grouper cannot tell if a condition started in hospital; hospital-acquired condition checks fail. What to do: Count and report missing POA by hospital. Some hospital types (for example critical access hospitals) are exempt from Medicare's POA payment rules.
lines.say: Missing or invalid P O A flag. What happens: The grouper cannot tell if a condition started in hospital; hospital-acquired condition checks fail. What to do: Count and report missing P O A by hospital. Some hospital types (for example critical access hospitals) are exempt from Medicare's P O A payment rules.

lines.raw: **Ungroupable claim**. What happens: Invalid principal diagnosis, impossible age or sex for a code, or missing data. MS-DRG puts it in DRG **999 (Ungroupable)**. What to do: Keep a count; fix the source data or exclude with a note.
lines.say: Ungroupable claim. What happens: Invalid principal diagnosis, impossible age or sex for a code, or missing data. M S DRG puts it in D R G 999 (Ungroupable). What to do: Keep a count; fix the source data or exclude with a note.

lines.raw: **Code not valid on that date**. What happens: A retired or not-yet-valid ICD-10 code is ignored or makes the claim ungroupable. What to do: Check codes against the code set for the service date.
lines.say: Code not valid on that date. What happens: A retired or not-yet-valid I C D 10 code is ignored or makes the claim ungroupable. What to do: Check codes against the code set for the service date.

lines.raw: **Missing secondary diagnoses**. What happens: Stays group to lower-severity DRGs. What to do: Compare the average number of diagnoses per stay by hospital.
lines.say: Missing secondary diagnoses. What happens: Stays group to lower-severity D R G's. What to do: Compare the average number of diagnoses per stay by hospital.

lines.say: Billed D R G versus regrouped D R G.

lines.raw: The hospital puts a DRG on its claim; payers and analysts often **regroup** the claim themselves.
lines.say: The hospital puts a D R G on its claim; payers and analysts often regroup the claim themselves.

lines.raw: If they differ, check the version and the codes; payers also audit DRGs ("DRG validation").

lines.say: Different systems with different numbers and meanings.

lines.say: Never mix them in one column or one trend.

lines.say: Problem 4: episodes that overlap or are cut short.

scenes.section: Problem 4: episodes that overlap or are cut short

lines.raw: **Overlap**: one claim can fit two episodes (an ER visit during both a knee replacement episode and a diabetes episode).
lines.say: Overlap: one claim can fit two episodes (an E R visit during both a knee replacement episode and a diabetes episode).

lines.raw: Use **priority or nesting rules** so each dollar is counted once.
lines.say: Use priority or nesting rules so each dollar is counted once.

lines.raw: **Incomplete windows**: an episode that ends on 9 December is not complete until its claims arrive.
lines.say: Incomplete windows: an episode that ends on 9 December is not complete until its claims arrive.

lines.raw: Leave enough **run-out** after the window ends before reporting.
lines.say: Leave enough run-out after the window ends before reporting.

lines.raw: **Eligibility gaps**: a member who leaves the plan mid-episode has missing care.
lines.say: Eligibility gaps: a member who leaves the plan mid-episode has missing care.

lines.raw: Flag or exclude those episodes.
lines.say: Flag or exclude those episodes.

lines.raw: MS-DRG versions change every 1 October, APCs every 1 January; use the claim-date version to check payments.

lines.raw: For trends over years, regroup all years with one version.

lines.raw: Missing POA, invalid codes and missing secondary diagnoses change groups; ungroupable stays go to DRG 999.

lines.raw: Combine interim bills before grouping; never mix MS-DRG and APR-DRG.
